implementation_notes: Play expresses the enforcer as action composition: an ActionBuilder (or ActionRefiner) in invokeBlock enforces authentication for every action it wraps and produces a request carrying the principal, so the protected surface is visible in controller signatures; the mechanism (token verification, OIDC, session lookup) is a service the builder calls. http4s and other typelevel stacks use the same shape as a middleware function HttpRoutes[F] => HttpRoutes[F]. No framework-level default-deny exists, so actions that use the plain Action remain public by construction.
pitfalls: Actions that use the plain Action instead of the authenticated builder are public; there is no global default-deny, so every controller must be inspected when auditing the protected surface.
Blocking token verification inside invokeBlock runs on Play's request execution context; use a non-blocking client or a dedicated dispatcher to avoid starving the default pool.
